newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian prosecutors tapped phones of top brass.
newsitem.headline: Colombian prosecutors tapped phones of top brass.

text.p: The telephones of six top Colombian generals were tapped over a three-month period starting in November of last year as part of a probe into the assassination of a leading politician, local news reports said on Sunday.

A report in El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, said the wiretaps were ordered by an investigator with the chief prosecutor's office as part of a probe into the killing of Alvaro Gomez, a three-time presidential candidate and outspoken critic of President Ernesto Samper.
Gomez was gunned down in the capital in broad daylight on Nov. 2 last year. The circumstances surrounding his murder, which shocked the nation, remain a mystery.
The presence of a military vehicle near the university campus where it occurred raised initial suspicions of a possible army connection to the crime, but this has never been confirmed.
According to El Tiempo, the officials whose phones were tapped for three months included Gen. Harold Bedoya, the former army chief who was promoted to armed forces commander by Samper just last week.

Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, the former army inspector general who won promotion last week to army commander, was another one of the generals whose telephone conversations were monitored by the chief prosecutor's office, the newspaper said.

It said Gen. Camilo Zuniga -- the armed forces commander who retired early this year amid reports that his U.S. travel visa had been revoked because of his alleged ties to drug traffickers -- was also among the targets of the wiretaps.
None of the officials named in the report were available for immediate comment.
